archetypes.name: python-bash-parity
archetypes.rationale: Parallel site-to-token mapping exists in both Python (checks.py) and bash (lint-fix-loop.sh); parity bugs silently misclassify ledger entries since tests exercise each language in isolation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the site-to-ledger-token mapping in Python (`_ledger_site_for_lint_site`, `_ledger_trigger_for_lint_site`, `_ledger_step_for_site`, `_ledger_phase_for_site` in `python/checks.py`) with the bash counterparts (`lint_fix_ledger_step`, `lint_fix_ledger_phase`, and `emit_lint_fix_ledger_ready` in `scripts/lint-fix-loop.sh`). Specifically check whether bash emits `LINT_FIX_LEDGER_SITE=$SITE` (raw value including `ship-pr-ci-initial`) while Python translates that site to `ship-pr-internal` via `_ledger_site_for_lint_site`, and whether the fallback branches differ (`unknown` in bash vs. `ci-merge`/`8` in Python). Verify whether `NEEDS_USER_SHIP_PR_INTERNAL_LINT_FIX` from `python/config.py` is the single source of truth for the `ship-pr-internal-lint-fix` string or whether a separate literal is used in bash. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: json-stdout-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan contract requires ship.py stdout to remain exactly one JSON object; the eight new ledger_* fields in to_json_dict() and the ledger_exit_code: int | None serialization must not break downstream consumers or create unexpected null JSON values.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect `python/ship.py` `ShipResult.to_json_dict()` and verify it still emits exactly one JSON object after the addition of eight new `ledger_*` fields. Check whether `ledger_exit_code: int | None` serializes to JSON null when None, and whether downstream callers in `skills/implement/SKILL.md` or test fixtures handle both integer and null values. Also examine the conditional at the `ShipResult` constructor call in `_step_result_to_ship` where `ledger_dispatcher=ledger_dispatcher if ledger_ready else ""` — confirm that non-escalation results with `ledger_ready=false` but all other `ledger_*` fields populated in JSON don't confuse consumers expecting the fields absent when `ledger_ready` is false. Verify the new tests in `python/test_ship.py` assert no extra stdout lines beyond the single JSON object. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
